newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans T$60 bln May/June T-bill to buy arms.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans T$60 bln May/June T-bill to buy arms.

text.p: Taiwan's Finance Ministry said on Friday it was planning to issue T$60 billion in treasury bills in May or June to finance the purchase of armaments.
Details of the issue had yet to be made final, Chang Hsiu-lien, head of the ministry's national treasury department, told reporters.
Chang said the T-bills could be issued in one or two tranches, the size and timing of which would be determined in accordance to Taiwan's liquidity situation in coming months, Chang said.
Chang declined to give further details about the issue or the weapons that would be purchased with the proceeds.

Nationalist-ruled Taiwan has ordered 150 F-16 fighters from the United States and 60 Mirage fighters from France -- worth nearly US$6 billion -- to bolster its defences against communist rival China, with deliveries starting in coming weeks.
It also is importing batteries of U.S. Patriot antimissile missiles and advanced Stinger missiles and six radar-deflecting "stealth" frigates from France.
The heavy arms purchases contributed to a record US$10.11 billion imports in March, the first time Taiwan's monthly imports had surpassed US$10 billion.
Officials attributed a big rise in March imports mainly to US$700 million in military outlays for the import of the first two of the six French-made Lafayette-class missile frigates.
The frigate order alone is costing Taiwan US$3 billion.
China, which has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a civil war split them in 1949, insists the island must be brought under mainland control -- by force if necessary.
